profit_question: Can I make the protocol believe inventory is worth more or less than it really is for one transaction?

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Dust-loop extraction via rounding differences across pool types
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All pool types round in favor of the pool. SingleProviderHelper uses mulDiv (rounds down for output) and mulDivRoundingUp (rounds up for input). DynamicPoolType delegates to concentrated liquidity math with same rounding convention. FullMath.mulDiv is 512-bit precision with no phantom overflow. Round-trip swap always loses dust to rounding, never gains.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: SingleProviderHelper.sol:calculateFixedInput (mulDiv rounds DOWN output), calculateFixedOutput (mulDivRoundingUp rounds UP input). FullMath.sol: 512-bit phantom overflow protection.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Flash loan fee token denomination mismatch
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Flash loan fee validation at AMMModule._executeTokenFlashloanHooks validates fee token is either the borrowed token or a configured cross-token fee payment. The _computeFlashLoanFee uses the same token's decimal precision. No denomination confusion possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: feeOnTop unsigned in permit SWAP_TYPEHASH enables executor theft
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: While feeOnTop is not signed, the signer sets limitAmount (minimum output) which IS signed. Any feeOnTop inflation reduces input to the swap, reducing output. If output drops below limitAmount, the transaction reverts. The signer is protected by their signed limitAmount.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: PermitTransferHandler.sol SWAP_TYPEHASH_STUB: feeOnTop absent from signed fields. AMMModule.sol:2225-2231: feeOnTop deducted from amountIn before swap. Limit check at finalization reverts if amountOut < limitAmount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Forged hook caller bypassing AMM authorization
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All hook entry points validate msg.sender == AMM address. AMMStandardHook has _requireCallerIsAMM() at lines 110, 159, 253, 312. SingleProviderPoolType has onlyAMM modifier on all external functions. CLOBTransferHandler checks msg.sender != AMM at lines 230, 316.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Transient storage cross-path theft between swap types
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Reentrancy guards (nonReentrantWithFlags) prevent concurrent swaps. DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) in hook contract's address space cannot collide with DIAMOND_STORAGE_QUEUED_FEE_COLLECT (0x9A1D...) in AMM's address space. Different contracts, different slot ranges.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Storage-slot collision in diamond proxy between modules
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All modules use Storage.appStorage() at slot 0x9A1D (diamond storage pattern). Reentrancy guard at keccak256-derived slot 0xeff970... in transient storage. Queued fees at 0x9A1D00000000... in transient storage. On cancun EVM, tstore/tload and sstore/sload are separate namespaces — no collision possible even at same slot number.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: LBAMMStorage.sol:29-31 (appStorage at DIAMOND_STORAGE_LBAMM_VAULT), TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:14 (REENTRANCY_GUARD_STORAGE), Tstorish.sol: separate tstore/sstore paths.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: snapPrice manipulation to distort pool pricing
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: DynamicPoolType.snapPrice guarded by liquidity > 0 check (reverts if pool has liquidity). Only works on empty pools. Additionally traverses tick bitmap to ensure no initialized ticks between current and target price. Cannot be used on active pools.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: DynamicHelper.sol:237-277 (snapPrice function), DynamicPoolType.sol:232-234 (liquidity check before snapPrice call).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: computeRatioX96 precision loss enabling price manipulation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 is only used for price bounds validation in _validatePricingBounds for direct swaps, not for actual pricing. Direct swap pricing is set by the executor (by design — OTC trades). Known issue CP-004 covers the case where afterSwap flag is disabled.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: SingleProviderPoolType hook-delegated pricing allows arbitrary price
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By design: the single provider is both the LP and hook operator. They price their own pool. Users are protected by limitAmount (minimum output). The AMM only validates price is within MIN/MAX_SQRT_RATIO mathematical bounds.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: SingleProviderPoolType.sol:306-370 (swapByInput with hook-delegated pricing), ISingleProviderPoolHook.sol (getPoolPriceForSwap interface).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fee asymmetry between input and output swap paths
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Lens 2 paired operation diff shows fee paths are symmetric within their respective economic contexts. Input swaps deduct fees from amountIn; output swaps add fees to amountIn. The shortage calculation formulas differ but are mathematically correct for their contexts (input path accounts for LP fee deduction, output path only accounts for hop fee).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Reentrancy during queued hook fee transfers causes fee loss
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: While _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers clears the reentrancy guard (line 3190) before executing transfers, the queue counter is already reset to 0. Re-entrant swaps could queue new fees that are never consumed, but the attacker doesn't profit — the hook's fees from the re-entrant swap are simply lost in transient storage at tx end. This is a potential low-severity fee-loss-to-hooks issue, NOT a price distortion vector.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: AMMModule.sol:3183-3204 (_executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers), line 3189 resets queue to 0, line 3190 clears guard.
